'UNIFY.C2 announced today that it has been selected as the Common Operating Picture platform for Counter-UAS and drone [detection]... at Beale Air Force Base' (June 2026) on a bootstrapped, ~12-14 person team with no external venture round → stage_pressure

blind_spots.blind_spot: 'Flexible: Cloud · GovCloud · On-prem' is pitched as a deployment-flexibility feature for the single-pane-of-glass COP
blind_spots.operator_reality: The site never addresses what happens to the unified picture when the link between a forward perimeter's radar/RF/EO-IR nodes and the central COP goes intermittent — their own stated failure mode ('operational friction at the moment clarity matters most') is exactly what DDIL causes, but the product framing treats connectivity as a deployment-location choice, not a battlefield condition to survive.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Marketing frames GovCloud/on-prem as customer preference options, not as a DDIL-resilience architecture question.

blind_spots.blind_spot: Fresh Beale AFB win ingests 'military grade and Commercial Off The Shelf sensors and effectors' into one base-network platform, with no visible compliance hire
blind_spots.operator_reality: A C2 platform that consolidates base perimeter sensor feeds needs an ATO/IL-level authorization before it can run on base networks at all — a 12-14 person, no-jobs-posted team suggests no dedicated ISSO/RMF owner shepherding that through for each new base, risking the exact fielding-clock problem Barry targets.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: No jobs data found in the pack at all, on a company that just won a new AFB deployment.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: UNIFY.C2 is an operationally deployed, sensor agnostic Counter UAS software platform built to integrate the widest range of military grade and Commercial Off The Shelf sensors and effectors in a single operational picture.

blind_spots.blind_spot: 'Role-based: Data segmentation by agency & geography' is marketed as a simple access-control config across '22 state, local, and federal' partners
blind_spots.operator_reality: Mixing DoD feeds (potentially CUI/classified) with civilian law-enforcement and homeland-security feeds inside one shared interoperability layer is a cross-domain-solution (CDS) problem, not a permissions toggle — CDS accreditation is one of the slowest, most failure-prone steps in fielding a multi-agency C2 platform.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The site's language treats multi-agency sharing as the product's core selling point rather than its core accreditation risk.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: UNIFY.C2 is designed for interoperability at scale and supports interagency Counter UAS initiatives across the Department of Defense and more than twenty two state, local, and federal p[artners]

opener_hook: Beale selected UNIFY.C2 as its Counter-UAS COP in June — with radar, RF, and EO/IR all routing through one node, what does the fallback picture look like if that link drops mid-track?
what_they_do: Sensor-agnostic Counter-UAS command-and-control software fusing radar/RF/EO-IR/acoustic feeds into one Common Operating Picture for base security, homeland security, and public-safety missions.
